title: The right to propose an edit to the Pattern Artifact is gated by holding at least 1% of circulating PATTERN
content:
A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1 opens the Root Edit process: "The Root Edit process begins with a PATTERN token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal. A PATTERN token holder must hold at least 1% of the circulating token supply to submit a proposal. The proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the 'Pattern Prime' category."

Three design choices are packed into one paragraph. First, **who may propose** is a property of token balance, not of role or election — the Agent's constitution is amendable only by its economic owners. Second, the threshold is expressed against *circulating* supply, so the bar moves with distribution rather than being a fixed number of tokens. Third, submission is **dual-channel**: a machine-readable draft in Powerhouse and a human-readable post in a designated public forum category.

The trade-off is the classic one for proposal thresholds. A meaningful floor prevents the review pipeline — which consumes scarce Operational Facilitator attention within a hard seven-day clock — from being flooded. But it also means that a well-reasoned proposal from a small holder has no procedural route at all; it must first persuade someone large enough to sponsor it.

The dual-channel requirement is what makes the rest of the process auditable: every later step in the routine protocol is defined as a *reply to the Forum post*, so the post is the canonical thread of record.
description: Proposal power is token-weighted rather than open, filtering spam but concentrating agenda-setting in large holders; submissions must appear in Powerhouse and on the Sky Forum.
